title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 57
paragraphs: Now the Gephyraeans, to whom the murderers of Hipparchus belonged, by their own account were originally descended from Eretria; but as I find by carrying inquiries back, they were Phoenicians of the company that came with Cadmus to the land now called Boeotia, and they lived in the district of Tanagra, which had been allotted to them in that land. Then, after the Cadmeians had first been driven out by the Argives, these Gephyraeans in turn were driven out by the Boeotians and made their way to Athens. The Athenians received them on certain fixed conditions to be citizens of their state, laying down rules that they should be excluded from a number of things not worth mentioning here.
